_comment: v3.66.1452. Re-run from a detached clone: toolchain/bin/bd-mutate --spec tests/mutants/v3_66_1452_shuffle_lane_containment.json --work DETACHED_CLONE. Every mutant is a REALISTIC regression of this cut rather than a syntactic poke: each one is a single edit a future session could plausibly make while believing it harmless, and each would silently turn the deterministic sanctioned lane into a shuffled one, or turn the advisory lane into a blocking one, or hollow out the control that proves the lane can fail. M4 is the one worth reading twice -- it makes an EARLY refusal fail-open, and a LATER refusal in the same tool then still returns exit 4, so a catcher that asserted only the exit code would report CAUGHT while the defect shipped. It is caught because the assertion also requires the refusal's own distinctive remedy text (CLAUDE.md A5: when several refusals share an exit code, assert the distinctive diagnostic).
